name: Li Andersson - Annexe I, § 11 - Am 36
title: REPORT on the proposal for a Council decision on guidelines for the employment policies of the Member States
part_text: As a complementary solution to tapping, as a priority, the potential of the Union domestic workforce, Member States may attract talent and skills from outside the Union via legal migration pathways strictly targeted at the proven needs of their labour market, while guaranteeing fair recruitment and labour and social rights. In accordance with Article 79(5) TFEU, Member States retain the right to determine volumes of admission of third-country nationals coming to their territory in order to seek work. Admission for employment purposes should be conditional upon a job offer or an employment contract corresponding to a proven labour shortage. Member States should ensure that procedures to recognise qualifications of third-country nationals in the context of legal migration procedures are simple, efficient and facilitate fast access to regulated professions, while maintaining quality standards. Any cooperation with third countries on labour mobility should be conditional upon their effective cooperation on the readmission of their nationals who are staying illegally. Member States should put in place a demanding integration policy, based on learning the language of the host country and on respect for its laws and for the values of the Union, and should be able to make access to certain support measures conditional upon effective participation in integration programmes. Member States should step up the fight against illegal employment of illegally staying third-country nationals, in particular through the effective application of Directive 2009/52/EC.
